data.narrative:
Proxima Fusion is a Series A-stage nuclear energy company that has raised €200M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 peers—3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Valar Atomics, Fuse Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Oklo, and X-Energy, representing the same sector and adjacent stages.

Two valuation methods apply here. Stage-progression analysis uses the €200M total raised as a proxy base ($1.4B equivalent), applying a typical Series A-to-next-stage multiplier of 2.0x, yielding $2.8B. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics ($6.0B, Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy ($808M, Seed), and Fuse Energy ($200M, Series A)—produces a median of $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects stage heterogeneity and capital intensity variance in the nuclear sector.

Triangulating these methods produces a valuation range of $687M (low) to $3.2B (high), with a median of $1.8B. The low-to-high spread reflects uncertainty around commercialization timelines, regulatory risk, and the substantial capital requirements typical of frontier nuclear technologies. The peer-median approach anchors toward the lower bound, while stage-progression suggests material step-up potential. Key uncertainties include technology validation speed and the trajectory of comparable funding rounds in this rapidly capitalizing sector.
